title: Machine States, Spaces, Cells, Shakes & Parts
description: Appliance cards that animate only while running, a container-query mail shell, per-glyph type motion, shake-to-summon shelves and skinnable headless elements.

drops.title: Machines That Show Their State
drops.description: Five appliance cards where the illustration is the status readout — the drum only tumbles while the cycle runs.
drops.concept: Home Assistant's appliance card packs have gone from icons to full animated illustrations: a tumbling washer drum, a flickering pellet flame, a bubbling hot tub, a blue burner crown. The trick worth stealing is that every keyframe is gated on a single data-state attribute, so 'running', 'standby' and 'finished' are one attribute swap rather than three variants of a component.

interaction.mouse: Hover a card to lift it; the panel sliders retime and re-intensify every animation at once.
interaction.click: Click any card to cycle it through running → standby → finished.
interaction.touch: Tap cards to change state; the tuning panel stacks above the grid.

drops.title: Spaces, Cards and a Today Pane
drops.description: A five-pane mail shell with a coloured spaces rail that reflows against its own width, not the viewport's.
drops.concept: Thunderbird's calmer themes have converged on one shell: an 88px spaces rail, a folder list, calm message cards with round avatars and hairline separators, and a full-height Today pane. Rebuilt here with container queries, so the panes leave in order — Today, then folders, then the toolbar collapses into » and the rail drops its labels — no matter where the component is embedded.
drops.source: sruf79/halo-spaces — a calm Thunderbird design for macOS

interaction.mouse: Drag the width slider to shrink the shell and watch the panes drop out in order.
interaction.click: Switch spaces in the rail, pick folders, select messages; toggle compact vs touch density.
interaction.touch: The shell keeps its own breakpoints on a phone; tap through spaces and messages.

drops.title: Type, Cell by Cell
drops.description: Every glyph becomes a cell carrying its own index, so six motion channels share three custom properties.
drops.concept: CellMotion treats each character, icon or media box as an independently animatable cell on a shared timeline rather than animating a whole text block. Split a string into spans that each carry --i, and stagger, duration and amplitude become three variables — six very different effects (rise, fold, shutter, scatter, wave, weight) then differ only by which @keyframes name they point at.
drops.source: opc8838-hub/font-animation (CellMotion) — editable motion for type, icons and media

interaction.mouse: Hover a lane and click to replay it; sliders retime every lane live.
interaction.click: Click any lane to restart its animation; type your own words in the panel.
interaction.touch: Tap lanes to replay; lanes also replay when they scroll back into view.

drops.title: Shake to Summon the Shelf
drops.description: Drag a file, shake the pointer, and a shelf flies in under the cursor to catch the drop.
drops.concept: DropShelf revives the Dropover gesture for Windows: while a drag is in flight, shaking the pointer — roughly six direction reversals inside 100 px — opens a temporary shelf at the cursor, with a dwell at the screen edge as the second trigger. Both are cheap to implement on pointer events, and the sensitivity really is just two numbers plus a rolling time window, which is why the app ships a calibration pad.
drops.source: wangmingkun148/DropShelf — a temporary file shelf for Windows

interaction.mouse: Press a card and drag, then shake — the charge meter fills and the shelf pops in; or hold at a screen edge.
interaction.click: Drop onto the shelf to stack it; flip stack/list view from its header; Esc dismisses.
interaction.touch: Drag with a finger and shake the same way; the shelf opens under your thumb.

drops.title: Behaviour Inside, Looks Outside
drops.description: Three custom elements that ship keyboard handling, ARIA and form participation — and no CSS at all.
drops.concept: Slab builds each web component on the native element it corresponds to and ships behaviour with no stylesheet, exposing styling hooks through ::part() and custom states through :state(). Rebuilt here without Lit: a switch, a stepper and a rating element whose internals set CustomStateSet entries, so a skin can write :state(at-max)::part(up) instead of remembering to toggle a class.
drops.source: ynotdraw/slab-elements — headless web components built on native elements

interaction.mouse: Toggle the switch, step the counter, set a rating — the same markup responds in all three columns.
interaction.click: Compare skins side by side; the live FormData readout proves the elements participate in forms.
interaction.touch: All three elements are tap- and keyboard-operable; arrow keys drive the stepper and rating.
